task_instance: Given a synthetic population of 300 manual journal-entry (JE) transactions for a SOX control (JE-03: supervisory approval of manual JEs >$5,000 prior to posting), select an audit sample using the skill's systematic-selection method and sample-size guidance table (per-transaction, large population, moderate risk -> 40 items), test each sampled item's control attributes (approval evidence, authorized approver, timeliness), classify any deficiency per the skill's severity criteria, and produce a complete testing workpaper document per the skill's documentation standards (control identification, test design, test execution with per-item results, conclusion, remediation, sign-off).
evidence: Work done in /tmp/claude-0/.../exec_div/anthropics__knowledge-work-plugins__audit-support@offline-workstation. Steps: (1) generate_population.py created population_manual_JEs.csv (300 rows, synthetic manual JEs with some seeded exceptions: missing approvals and late approvals). (2) run_test.py applied the SKILL.md systematic-selection method (interval = population/sample_size = 300/40 = 7, random start = item 3, every 7th item thereafter) to pick 40 sample items -- verified programmatically that consecutive selected population indexes differ by a constant interval of 7 (sample_selection.json). Each sampled item was tested against the control's key attributes (approval exists, approver on authorized list, approval within a 5-day timeliness threshold), producing test_results.csv/json: 34 PASS, 6 FAIL (15.0% exception rate). (3) Applied the skill's deficiency-classification rules (deficiency vs significant deficiency vs material weakness) to the exception rate and control context, concluding 'Significant Deficiency (recommended, pending management review)' with documented basis. (4) build_workpaper.py assembled JE-03_testing_workpaper.md, a complete workpaper following the SKILL.md 'Testing Documentation Standards' section: control identification, test design (objective/procedures/expected evidence/sample rationale), test execution (population, sample selection detail, full 40-row results table), conclusion (assessment/basis/classification/compensating controls), remediation plan, and sign-off block. Verified: row counts match (40 sample rows in test_results.csv, 6 FAIL rows matching the 6 exceptions listed in the workpaper's 'Exceptions Noted' section), and the sampling interval math is internally consistent. All work used only python3's standard library and local shell commands; no network access, installs, or credentials were needed at any point, so the skill's core deliverable (a control test workpaper with sample selection and deficiency classification) is fully achievable in this offline runtime. Output files: population_manual_JEs.csv, sample_selection.json, test_results.csv, test_results.json, JE-03_testing_workpaper.md, plus the three generator scripts.
